primitives.verbatim_quote: Brooks, of the Johns Hopkins University, told me of his large and noble dog being frightened into a sort of epileptic fit by a bone being drawn across the floor by a thread which the dog did not see.

primitives.name: Corpse-Induced Instinctive Dread
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the witch and hobgoblin supernatural, other elements still of fear are brought in—caverns, slime and ooze, vermin, corpses, and the like.† A human corpse seems normally to produce an instinctive dread,which is no doubt somewhat due to its mysteriousness, and which familiarity rapidly dispels.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_{\\text{corpse}}': 'dimensionless dread from corpse exposure', 'M_{\\text{mystery}}': 'mystery factor of corpse visibility', 'F_{\\text{familiarity}}': 'familiarity decay rate'}
primitives.assumptions: Instinctive dread correlates with mystery and inversely with familiarity.

layer2.mapping: State transition kernel in GSE modeling dread onset; likelihood function in GSI for dread classification.
layer2.telemetry: Autonomic nervous system response and avoidance behavior metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The three primitives form a hierarchical fear response model: sensory deception triggers immediate fear through perceptual mismatch, ancestral memory activates supernatural dread through evolutionary replay, and corpse exposure induces instinctive dread via mystery and familiarity thresholds. These interact through a shared latent variable space of fear intensity and memory depth. The dualities lie in the contrast between conscious control (sensory deception) and unconscious inheritance (ancestral memory), while failure modes include false positives in fear detection and memory misattribution. The model supports retroactive inference of fear origins and future risk prediction.
